First, let's establish the base rate for the S&P 500 decreasing by over 5% in one day (close-to-close).
Historically, a 5% daily drop in the S&P 500 is a very rare event.
Looking at historical data since 1950:
- 1987 Black Monday: -20.4%
- 2008 Financial Crisis: -9.0% (Oct 15), -8.8% (Oct 9), -7.6% (Dec 1), etc.
- 2020 COVID crash: -11.98% (Mar 16), -9.51% (Mar 12), -7.6% (Mar 9)
There are very few days with a >5% close-to-close drop.
Out of roughly 18,000 trading days since 1950, there have been about 15-20 days with a >5% drop.
